newsitem.title: CHINA: Taiwan diplomatic partners shut Hong Kong missions.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan diplomatic partners shut Hong Kong missions.

text.p: Most countries with diplomatic links to Taiwan have shut their Hong Kong consulates in line with China's demand that they be closed after Beijing resumed sovereignty here on July 1, officials said on Thursday.
Communist-ruled China regards arch-rival Taiwan as a renegade province instead of a separate nation, and opposes it establishing diplomatic relations with other countries.

Nationalist-ruled Taiwan has only 30 diplomatic partners, mostly poor Latin American or African nations, after fighting a losing battle with China for diplomatic recognition since the two split in 1949 after the communist victory in the Chinese civil war.
That number will fall to 29 next year when South Africa, Taipei's largest ally, switches formal recognition to Beijing.

The consulates of St Kitts & Nevis, Senegal, Tonga and the Dominican Republic shut down on June 30, just before Hong Kong was handed back to China following 156 years as a British colony, an official said, quoting the latest records on the diplomatic corps.
The Belize consulate closed after the handover. The consulates of Tonga, Belize and the Dominican Republic have been turned into trade offices.
Panama, Costa Rica and Paraguay shut their consulates in June. The Central African Republic's mission shut down in January.
Other consulates closed last year or even prior to that.
Some countries with a diplomatic link to Taiwan, including South Africa and Liberia, still keep their consulates.

China has allowed South Africa to keep its consulate open in Hong Kong following diplomatic recognition of China by Pretoria last November and a pledge by President Nelson Mandela gradually to establish full diplomatic links by January 1998.
